newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge leader supports Cambodian royalists.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge leader supports Cambodian royalists.

text.p: The Khmer Rouge's nominal leader, Khieu Samphan, said on Wednesday his new party supported a political alliance set up by Cambodian First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
The move could exacerbate friction between Ranariddh and Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, his partner in an uneasy coalition government formed in 1993, analysts said.
Ranariddh on Monday had offered Khieu Samphan's National Solidarity Party a "very great welcome" to the prince's National United Front (NUF) alliance.

Khieu Samphan said in a radio broadcast monitored in Phnom Penh: "I would like to declare that the National Solidarity Party continues to help and support the National United Front, other political parties, politicians who respect and implement the 14-point platform of the National United Front to end the war."
The NUF includes Ranariddh's royalist FUNCINPEC party, the opposition Khmer Nation Party and a wing of the small Buddhist Liberal Democratic Party (BLDP).
Analysts said the announcements by the prince and Khieu Samphan indicated they were ready to join forces politically.
The NUF is seen as an alliance against FUNCINPEC's rival and coalition partner, the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) of Hun Sen.
The prince said Khieu Samphan wanted to establish a party excluding Khmer Rouge hardliners such as Ta Mok, Son Sen and Pol Pot, ultimate leader of the Maoist group.
Ranariddh and Hun Sen have competed to win Khmer Rouge support since the guerrilla movement began falling apart after the defection of former top official Ieng Sary late last year.
The Maoist-inspired Khmer Rouge, whose genocidal 1975-79 rule left more than one million people dead, signed a U.N.-brokered peace pact with rival Cambodian factions in 1991.

But the group reneged on the accord and had been fighting the current coalition government formed after U.N.-run elections in 1993. A core of fewer than 2,000 guerrillas still holds out against the government in northern Cambodia.
Hun Sen warned on Monday that the Khmer Rouge could still come to power through political rather than military means.
